clue.text: Things needed in cold hotels, possibly

parts.note: C is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

indicators.note: possibly suggests the hotels could be rearranged into some other form

explanation.surface: A remark on what guests need to bring when staying in chilly hotels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges C (cold) with HOTELS. 'needed in' only links; the surface makes 'Things needed in cold' look like one definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Your things, in casual speech, are your garments and belongings, as in 'put your things on'.

clue.text: Egyptian king starts eating cutlets outside!

indicators.note: outside puts the cutlets around the first letter of eating

parts.note: chops are cutlets of meat

indicators.note: starts takes only the opening letter of eating

explanation.surface: A pharaoh tucks into his cutlets, the exclamation mark adding glee.
explanation.walkthrough: Cheops, also called Khufu, built the Great Pyramid of Giza.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheops was a pharaoh of the Fourth Dynasty, a ruler of ancient Egypt.

clue.text: Offer more for a lot?

parts.note: a lot looks like a large amount, but at auction it is an item for sale, and offering more than a rival wins it

explanation.surface: Someone tempted to pay a lot more for something.
explanation.definitionFit: At an auction, a bidder who tops a rival's offer beats them to the item.

clue.text: Strapping on skull produces rash

indicators.note: on in a down clue places the strapping word below the skull word

parts.note: the skull is the head
a strapping person is big and strong

explanation.surface: Fastening something to one's head gives rise to a skin rash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rash' looks like a skin complaint but is the adjective meaning reckless.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone wilful and impetuous acts without thought, determined to get their own way.

clue.text: Second stroke causes laceration

parts.note: a lash is a stroke of a whip

explanation.surface: A second blow of a whip leaves a wound.
explanation.definitionFit: A gash or long cut, such as a knife makes, is a laceration.

clue.text: One legislator for every single challenge…

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
an MP, Member of Parliament, makes laws
each means for every single one

explanation.surface: Each lawmaker poses a challenge, with the ellipsis leading into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: MP is a Member of Parliament, the British legislature.
explanation.definitionFit: To impeach an official is to formally challenge their conduct or call their integrity into question.

clue.text: I am on time at university but unprepared

parts.note: I'm is the contraction of I am
prompt means punctual

explanation.surface: A student says they were punctual at college but had not done the work.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done off the cuff, without rehearsal, is improvised.

clue.text: Perform quiet song?

parts.note: P is piano, the musical marking for quiet
a lay is a ballad or song

explanation.surface: A singer is asked to perform a soft song.
explanation.definitionFit: To act a role or give a musical performance is to play.

clue.text: Giving guarantee with a vessel that is put on universal hotplate?

indicators.note: put on in a down clue sets the first pieces on top of the rest

parts.note: SS is a steamship
U is the film rating meaning universal
a ring is a burner on a cooker

explanation.surface: Someone vows a pot will be set on the cooker ring.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the British film certificate for universal viewing; a ring is a hob burner. 'that is' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Assuring someone means promising or pledging that something is so.

clue.text: Times for making hay on lidos?

indicators.note: making signals that these letters are made into something new

explanation.surface: Sunbathers making hay while the sun shines at outdoor pools.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making' rearranges HAY and LIDOS; 'on' only links. A lido is an open-air swimming pool.
explanation.definitionFit: Vacations are periods of leisure, the season for relaxation.

clue.text: … or more in this context, raffishly

indicators.note: in tells us the letters sit inside the run of words context and raffishly

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue, it muses on a word used in a rakish context.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis joins this clue to the one before; 'or' is just a link and 'this' points to the words that follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra as an adverb or adjective means additional, beyond the usual amount.

clue.text: Opinion of lift, unfinished, in papal trip?

indicators.note: in places the shortened lift inside the rearranged papal letters
a trip is a stumble, so the letters of papal tumble into a new order
unfinished drops the final letter of the synonym for lift

parts.note: to lift something is to raise it

explanation.surface: A view on a pope's journey and how he raised spirits on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trip' turns PAPAL into APP...AL; 'unfinished' cuts RAISE to RAIS, which goes 'in' between them.
explanation.definitionFit: An appraisal is an assessment or considered judgement of something's worth.

clue.text: Pooh's tired out making all these revs

indicators.note: out signals the letters are thrown out of their order, as in being knocked out

parts.note: the bear's name with its S kept as a letter

explanation.surface: Winnie-the-Pooh is worn out by a crowd of clergymen.
explanation.walkthrough: Here the S of 'Pooh's' counts as a letter of the anagram, with TIRED. 'revs' is short for Reverends, clergymen.
explanation.definitionFit: Reverends collectively form the clergy, the body of ordained ministers.

clue.text: A clear desert

parts.note: to rid a place of something is to clear it

explanation.surface: A clear desert landscape, empty of anything.
explanation.definitionFit: Desert used as an adjective describes barren, waterless land, as in a desert island.

clue.text: Spider-crab, unusually, has a thin biscuit

indicators.note: unusually says the letters of spider-crab appear in an odd order

explanation.surface: A crab with long legs is oddly eating a cracker.
explanation.definitionFit: A crisp, flat rye wafer is eaten like a cracker.

clue.text: Photograph of Sheerness?

explanation.surface: A snapshot of the Kentish town of Sheerness.
explanation.walkthrough: Sheerness is a port town in Kent; here it is read as the quality of being sheer.
explanation.definitionFit: A slide or positive photograph on film is so named; sheer fabric has the property of letting light through.

clue.text: Peach providing heavenly drink in the orient

parts.note: nectar was the drink of the gods
the orient is the east, E

explanation.surface: A peach yields a divine drink in the Far East.
explanation.definitionFit: This smooth-skinned fruit is a variety of peach.

clue.text: Pearlies'exotic tree trainer

indicators.note: exotic suggests something foreign and strange, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Cockney pearly kings own a strange gadget for shaping trees.
explanation.walkthrough: Pearlies are London's pearly kings and queens, costermongers in button-covered clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A trellis or frame on which fruit trees are trained to grow flat.

clue.text: Large reptile works in bloomers

parts.note: croc is short for crocodile, a large reptile
uses means employs or works

explanation.surface: A crocodile at work wearing frilly bloomers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomers' suggests underwear; here it means plants that bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: Spring flowers grown from corms are things that bloom.

clue.text: Spaghetti part of meal found in raised line of bricks on building

definitions.text: raised line of bricks on building

parts.note: spaghetti is pasta in long thin strings
a course is one stage of a meal, like soup or dessert

explanation.surface: A diner finds pasta from one stage of dinner stuck in the brickwork.
explanation.definitionFit: Builders use the term for a horizontal band of projecting brick or stone along a facade.

clue.text: Creator of "The Goldenheaded God"?

indicators.note: headed says the gold symbol comes at the head of the god

parts.note: AU is the chemical symbol for gold
Thor is the Norse god of thunder

explanation.surface: Who wrote a book called The Goldenheaded God?
explanation.definitionFit: A writer creates a book, so is its creator.

clue.text: Unaffected by being hounded, we hear

indicators.note: we hear means the word for hounded is spoken aloud

parts.note: to be hounded is to be chased

explanation.surface: Someone untroubled by being pursued by others.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaste can mean simple and unadorned, free of pretension.

clue.text: Pre-eminent architectural feature

explanation.surface: An outstanding element of a building.
explanation.definitionFit: As a prefix or adjective it means chief or principal, as in archenemy; it is also a curved span over an opening.

clue.text: With which Turner depicted a ship, burnt and wrecked?

definitions.text: With which Turner depicted a ship, burnt and wrecked?

indicators.note: a wrecked vessel breaks up, so these letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: J. M. W. Turner, the painter, recording a burning shipwreck on canvas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrecked' rearranges A SHIP BURNT. Turner, the English painter of sea scenes, made the whole clue a definition too.
explanation.definitionFit: A painter applies colour with a hand tool of bristles on a handle.

clue.text: Corner of scenic Henley

indicators.note: of means the letters are taken out of the words scenic Henley

explanation.surface: A nook in picturesque Henley, the Thames rowing town.
explanation.walkthrough: Henley-on-Thames is an English riverside town famous for its regatta.
explanation.definitionFit: A niche is a recess or nook, such as a corner.

clue.text: Pass over main road in outskirts of Oscroft

indicators.note: in places the motorway inside the outer letters of Oscroft
outskirts of takes the first and last letters of Oscroft

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's main motorway, written MI

explanation.surface: Driving past the M1 on the edge of a village called Oscroft.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the motorway from London to Leeds; its 1 is read as I.
explanation.definitionFit: To omit something is to skip or leave it out.

clue.text: Woolly jumper counter?

parts.note: woolly jumpers are sheep leaping a fence, and counting them is the classic remedy for someone who cannot sleep

explanation.surface: Someone tallying knitted sweaters in a shop.
explanation.walkthrough: A jumper is the British word for a sweater; here it is a sheep that jumps.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who lies awake all night is said to count sheep in the hope of dropping off.

clue.text: Spirit of those in revolt

indicators.note: in revolt means overturned, so the letters of those are rearranged

explanation.surface: The fighting spirit of people who rise up against authority.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethos is the characteristic spirit or guiding beliefs of a community.

clue.text: One may be buttonholed for a favour

definitions.text: One may be buttonholed for a favour

parts.words: One may be buttonholed for a favour
parts.note: buttonholed seems to mean cornered to ask a favour, but means pinned to a lapel buttonhole as a ribbon favour

explanation.surface: Someone is collared by an acquaintance wanting help.
explanation.walkthrough: A favour here is a ribbon badge worn as a token, not a kindness.
explanation.definitionFit: A gathered ribbon badge is worn on the lapel as a prize or party emblem.

clue.text: Back last runner 'ome!

parts.note: the end is the last part

indicators.note: home said with the h dropped shows the h must go from the runner

parts.note: a horse is a runner in a race

explanation.surface: A punter backs the final horse home at the racecourse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ome, home with a Cockney dropped H, tells you to drop the H of HORSE to give ORSE.
explanation.definitionFit: To endorse a candidate or plan is to support it.
